title: The Resignation Letter
summary: Captain Maer resigned rather than burn a village. She still has the letter she was ordered to deliver. She never delivered it. She is not sure what to do about that — or the village, which is still standing, and still exposed.

phases.label: Maer describes the order she refused

onComplete.text: 'The order cited cult-sympathizer grounds. The assessment was mine. I wrote it three months earlier about general Ashen Veil activity in the area — not about that village specifically. Someone used it anyway.' She does not use the word 'falsified.' She uses 'repurposed.' The distinction is exact.

phases.label: Locate the village and assess its current situation

onComplete.text: Fenwold is intact. Forty-three people. A watermill. A blacksmith who sharpens the shrine-keeper's tools at no charge. The Emberguard has not followed through — whether from resource shortage or because they assumed Maer complied, they cannot know. The village does not know about the order.

phases.label: Decide whether to warn the village and how

onComplete.text: A decision with weight. The village is still here. Whatever comes next, Maer made a different choice — and so did the party.

phases.label: Maer decides what to do about the letter and the chain of command that generated it

onComplete.text: She burns the letter. 'The letter was never the problem.' She keeps the assessment. 'The assessment is accurate. Someone needs to read it correctly.'
